The relevant work now has both a fixed product flow and a version-bound source assessment of the selected baseline. The delivery baseline remains `taggable-server` / `auto-50-perc-off` from prod commit `45826e12cdc8f585e514d7bb09c0d37fa28ed568`, but the latest assessment inspected that committed tree rather than executing from a checked-out `auto-50-perc-off` worktree; the active worktree was still `feature/kiosk-square-return-recovery`. That distinction matters: the assessment gives source-level capability and missing-connection evidence for the committed baseline, not live checkout behavior or deployment proof.

The Taggable product delivery flow remains unchanged: at an eligible current-tour checkout, use the existing face-recognition flow to establish the same person; obtain prior purchase evidence; qualify a paid purchase at any one configured prerequisite tour; locate an applicable existing 50% discount code for the current tour or location; and apply it to the order before payment while keeping checkout/search/payment behavior otherwise unchanged.

What is now source-supported on the inspected committed baseline: customer checkout/payment routes exist; checkout can read a supplied redeem-code cookie; the checkout view can preview an entered or saved code; and `postPayment` persists discount fields and increments discount uses before provider handling. `ProductDiscount` exists as a model surface with fields and relations relevant to later selector/application work. Existing recognition source surfaces also exist, including `AmazonFaceRecognitionService::searchFacesByImage`, but the assessment warns that recognition outputs and stored identifiers are not yet reconciled into the required same-person paid-prerequisite qualification.

What is demonstrably missing in the inspected source: the directed current-tour-to-prerequisite-tour storage/reader, historical purchase-evidence services such as `RecognitionPurchaseEvidence` and `SearchPaymentEvidence`, and an automatic 50% selector. The existing cookie/redeem-code automation is supplied-code handling, not automatic discovery based on prerequisite eligibility. Therefore the practical flow cannot start by assuming historical atoms are already installed; it should treat prerequisite storage/reader restoration as the first supported implementation boundary, with later qualification, selector, checkout application, and validation still separate.

The usable capability map is therefore: available baseline evidence is a committed-tree source assessment for `auto-50-perc-off` at `45826e12...`; available existing product surfaces include customer checkout/payment routes, supplied-code discount preview/persistence, `ProductDiscount`, and recognition helper behavior; historical bounded product source material remains useful provenance for prerequisite, eligibility, recognition/payment evidence, and selector work; partly built/proposed capability is the documented prerequisite restoration boundary with inputs, outputs, acceptance cases, and protected behavior; missing capability is the integrated automatic-discount sequence; and assumed future dependencies remain configured prerequisite rows, eligible 50% discount codes, recognition/search/payment linkage, database compatibility, checkout integration before payment, tests through the real path, and runtime/deployment validation.

Affected consumers remain checkout before payment, discount preview/payment persistence, face-recognition/search, purchase/payment evidence resolution, prerequisite eligibility, discount-code selection and usage guarding, owner review, and later atom/build machinery if used. The use-what-already-works lens should reuse the inspected source surfaces and historical atom records, but should not treat source inspection, proposed acceptance cases, or hash-verified historical artifacts as fresh passing product tests.
